content_metadata.description: This educational video explains the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, a key tool in astronomy. It provides a clear and engaging explanation of the diagram's components, star evolution, and age determination of star clusters, making complex concepts accessible through visuals and relatable examples.

qAndA.answer: The horizontal axis represents the color of stars (blue to red), while the vertical axis represents brightness (faint to bright).
qAndA.question: How are the axes of the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram labeled?
What is the name of the region on the HR diagram where most stars are located?

qAndA.answer: They fuse helium into heavier elements.
qAndA.question: What energy source do stars on the Giant Branch primarily use?

qAndA.answer: It expands into a red giant, then eventually collapses into a white dwarf.
qAndA.question: What happens to the Sun when it runs out of hydrogen fuel?

qAndA.answer: By identifying the 'turnoff point,' which indicates the point on the Main Sequence where stars have begun to evolve off and become giants, giving an estimate of the cluster's age.
qAndA.question: How can the HR diagram be used to determine the age of a star cluster?

youtube_description:
Chris Lintott and Rob Simpson from the Astrophysics Department discuss the influential Hertzsprung-Russell diagram which maps stars by luminosity and colour.
 
This video is part of the Exploring the Universe online short course offered by the Department for Continuing Education. See  http://www.conted.ox.ac.uk/F990-1 for more information.
